cheng: Heads-up: seeing periodic p99 tail surges in prod when concurrency climbs past ~2k. Correlation looks strong with KV cache eviction churn when microbatch sizes creep above 32.
amelia: yup noticed that on the latency dashboard — p95 steady (~120ms) but p99 jumps to ~420ms during spikes.
raj: is this the kernel-selection path that falls back to the generic kernel under pressure?
cheng: seems like it. Trace shows ~30-40ms added in kernel select + a burst of cache evictions that cause extra KV lookups. profiling-bot uploaded flamegraph.
profiling-bot: profile://uploads/1873456789/flamegraph.svg (heat on kernel_select + kv_evict_worker)
sophie: can you paste the quick numbers from the experiment matrix? microbatch 16/32/64 and evict rates?
cheng: sure — roughs from the canary run yesterday: 
```
mb=16 -> p95 110ms, p99 180ms, evict_rate 4/min
mb=32 -> p95 125ms, p99 420ms, evict_rate 21/min
mb=64 -> p95 160ms, p99 630ms, evict_rate 48/min
```
amelia: wow that evict_rate jump at 32->64 is dramatic. looks like KV capacity + chiming eviction windows.
raj: what's the current eviction_threshold? and are we doing async evict or inline?
cheng: threshold=0.75 currently, evict is async but we see worker saturation — eviction backlog causes delayed frees so new requests hit cold misses. Also kernel selector is choosing a slower fallback when seq distribution shifts.
sophie: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily raise threshold to 0.9 to reduce churn, 2) bias kernel selector to prefer fused kernels for seq<256 even if measured throughput slightly lower. That may reduce kernel-select overhead.
amelia: I'll approve a 1% canary for threshold bump if we add an alert: evict_rate>30/min OR p99>500ms -> rollback.
cheng: created canary rollout: bump eviction_threshold->0.9 on cluster-2 (1% traffic). watch keys: evict_rate, kernel_select_time, p99_tail.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed to cluster-2 (1% traffic) by amelia — rollout id r-2026-03-17-01
raj: note tradeoff: higher threshold increases memory pressure and slightly lowers throughput per-GPU, so cost may go up. we should measure token/sec decline.
sophie: also logging note: add a small metric for "kernel_fallback_rate" (count of times selector chooses fallback kernel) — should be visible in <1h.
cheng: agreed. I pushed a short-term dashboard with those panels and a synthetic probe that injects short sequences to exercise fused kernels.
amelia: monitoring looks clean first 10m: p99 down to 210ms on canary, evict_rate 9/min. will let it run 30m then decide. :thumbsup:
raj: if that holds, next step is to experiment with dynamic microbatch target: prefer smaller mb under high concurrency to keep evict pressure low, and increase when idle.
sophie: yes — a load-aware mb controller + quick kernel-hint should be the long-term fix. we should also profile kernel_select path to shave off the 20-40ms.
cheng: filing a follow-up perf ticket with traces and suggested controller design. Ticket: PERF-8721. I'll include exact perf counter dumps and the flamegraphs.
profiling-bot: attached PERF-8721 artifacts: /artifacts/8721/{cpu_samples,kv-stats,selector-traces}.tar.gz
amelia: thanks — keeping this thread pinned. will report final canary result in 30m.
cheng: thanks team — appreciate the quick loop.
